FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

 

Creative Realities Reports Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results

 

Revenue $26.2 Million, on Track for Record-Setting Year, Strong Outlook for 2027

 

LOUISVILLE, KY – November 16, 2026 – Creative Realities, Inc. (“Creative Realities,” “CRI,” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: CREX), a leading provider of digital signage, media and AdTech solutions, today announced its financial results for the fiscal third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

 

Highlights: 

 

 

●

Third quarter revenue of $26.2 million versus $10.5 million in the prior-year period.

 

 

●

Gross profit of $9.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 versus $4.8 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

 

 

●

Adjusted EBITDA* of $2.7 million for the third quarter of 2026 versus $0.8 million in the prior-year period.

 

 

●

Annualized recurring revenue (“ARR”)** of approximately $21.7 million at the end of the third quarter versus $12.3 million as of September 30, 2025.

 

 

●

Creative Realities announced that it has been selected by Zaxby’s, with over 1,000 locations across the United States, for digital media upgrades. Currently every location with previously-installed drive-through signage has been converted and is utilizing the Clarity CMS solution.

 

 

●

The previously-announced contract with Albertsons is currently on track, with CRI’s retail media network already deployed at 500+ stores – with roughly 15 screens per location now delivering over 30 million ads daily. All remaining stores are expected to be up and running with Creative Realities’ AdTech technology by the end of the second quarter 2027.

 

“We continue to set new records this year in terms of growth acceleration, business wins, and EBITDA expansion,” said Rick Mills, Chief Executive Officer. “We anticipate revenue exceeding $100 million in fiscal 2026, as the fourth quarter is expected to benefit from seasonal factors related to our retail media contracts as well as from the positive impact of recent awards and new customer installations. In addition to our significant work for Albertsons, the installation of our digital solutions at the new Tennessee Titans stadium is well underway and expected to be substantially completed by year end. We focused on the balance sheet this quarter, using existing cash to pay down debt, provide increased financial flexibility, and reduce ongoing interest expense. Our talented staff and leadership successfully executed an operating strategy that is producing significant growth as we become a more nimble organization intent on achieving improved bottom line results and cash generation. We are well on our way to our best year ever, with even greater performance anticipated for 2027.”

 

*Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure. A reconciliation is provided in the tables of this press release.

**Annualized Recurring Revenue, or ARR, is a non-GAAP operating metric that is described below.

 

2026 Third Quarter Financial Results

 

Sales were $26.2 million for the fiscal 2026 third quarter as compared to $10.5 million in the same period in fiscal 2025, with approximately $8.0 million in the current year quarter from the operations of our subsidiary, Cineplex Digital Media (“CDM”). Hardware sales rose to $11.4 million, versus $4.2 million in the prior-year period, while service revenue climbed to $14.9 million from $6.4 million in fiscal 2025, reflecting the CDM operations as well as deployment timing. Both revenue streams benefitted from recent wins and overall deployment timing.

 

Consolidated gross profit was $9.7 million for the fiscal 2026 third quarter versus $4.8 million in the prior-year period, and consolidated gross margin was 37.1% versus 45.3% in the fiscal 2025 third quarter. Gross margin on hardware revenue was 18.5% in fiscal 2026 as compared to 30.0% in the prior-year period, while gross margin on services amounted to 51.4% versus 55.3% in the fiscal 2025 third quarter. Hardware gross margin decreased year-over-year primarily due to mix, while service gross margin declined due to the expiration of certain customer contracts in 2025. The Company ended the 2026 third quarter with ARR of approximately $21.7 million. 

 

 

Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter rose to $2.8 million, versus $1.4 million in the prior-year period, while general and administrative (G&A) expenses increased to $9.3 million versus $5.0 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025, primarily as a result of the inclusion of CDM’s operations.

 

The Company posted an operating loss of approximately $2.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to an operating loss of $7.3 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025; the prior-year period included a software impairment charge of $5.7 million. CRI reported a net loss of $3.6 million and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $4.0 million, or $(0.29) per diluted share, in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 versus a net loss of $7.9 million, or $(0.75) per diluted share, in the prior-year period, including the aforementioned software impairment charge.

 

Adjusted EBITDA (defined later in this release) was $2.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $0.8 million in the prior-year period.

 

Balance Sheet

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash on hand of approximately $1.8 million, versus $1.6 million at December 31, 2025. The Company had outstanding debt of approximately $40.0 million versus $44.0 million at the start of the fiscal year.

 

Conference Call Details

The Company will host a conference call to review the results of the third quarter of 2026, and provide additional commentary about recent performance, today, November 16, at 9:00 am Eastern Time, which will include prepared remarks and materials from management, followed by a live Q&A. The call will be hosted by Rick Mills, Chief Executive Officer, and Tamra Koshewa, Chief Financial Officer,.

 

Prior to the call, participants should register at https://bit.ly/CREXearnings3Q2026. Once registered, participants can use the weblink provided in the registration email to participate in the live webcast. An archived edition of the earnings conference call will be posted on the Company’s website after the call and will remain available for one year.

 

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

The Company prepares its consolidated financial statements in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). In addition to disclosing financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, the Company discloses information regarding “EBITDA” and “Adjusted EBITDA.” The Company defines “EBITDA” as earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization of intangibles. The Company defines “Adjusted EBITDA” as EBITDA excluding stock-based compensation, fair value adjustments and both cash and non-cash non-recurring gains and charges. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are not measures of performance defined in accordance with GAAP. However, EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are used internally in planning and evaluating the Company’s operating performance. Accordingly, management believes that disclosure of these metrics offers investors, bankers and other stakeholders an additional view of the Company’s operations that, when coupled with the GAAP results, provides a more complete understanding of the Company’s financial results. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to net income/(loss) or to net cash used in operating activities as measures of operating results or liquidity. Our calculation of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies, and the measures exclude financial information that some may consider important in evaluating the Company’s performance. A reconciliation of GAAP net income/(loss) to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA is included in the accompanying financial schedules. For further information, please refer to the Company’s filings available online at www.sec.gov, including its Annual Report on Form 10-K for 2025 filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

 

Annualized recurring revenue, or “ARR,” represents the annualized revenue run rate of our subscription (1) software-as-a-service (“SaaS”) contracts, (2) maintenance and support of perpetual license contracts, and (3) content management service contracts at the end of the final calendar month included in a reporting period, assuming these contracts are renewed on their existing terms for customers that are under subscription contracts with us. This gives us an indication of the revenue that can be earned in the following 12-month period from our existing client base, assuming no cancellations or price changes occur during that period. We believe that ARR is a key operating metric to measure our business because it is driven by our ability to acquire new subscription customers and to maintain and expand our relationship with existing subscription customers. ARR should be viewed independently of revenue and deferred revenue as ARR is a performance metric and is not intended to be combined with any of these items.

 

For further information, please refer to the Company’s filings available online at www.sec.gov, including its Annual Report on Form 10-K for 2025 filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

 

 

About Creative Realities, Inc.

Creative Realities designs, develops and deploys digital signage-based experiences for enterprise-level networks utilizing its Clarity™, ReflectView™, and iShowroom™ Content Management System (CMS) platforms. The Company is actively providing recurring SaaS and support services across diverse vertical markets, including, but not limited to, retail, automotive, digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising networks, convenience stores, foodservice/QSR, gaming, theater, and stadium venues. In addition, the Company assists clients in utilizing place-based digital media to achieve business objectives such as increased revenue, enhanced customer experiences, and improved productivity. This includes the design, deployment, and day-to-day management of retail media networks to monetize on-premise foot traffic utilizing its AdLogic™ and CPM+™ programmatic advertising platforms.

RECONCILIATION OF GAAP NET LOSS TO ADJUSTED EBITDA

(in thousands, unaudited)

 

Creative Realities, Inc. prepares its consolidated financial statements in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). In addition to disclosing financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, the Company discloses information regarding “EBITDA” and “Adjusted EBITDA.” CRI defines “EBITDA” as earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization of intangibles. CRI defines “Adjusted EBITDA” as EBITDA excluding stock-based compensation, fair value adjustments and both cash and non-cash non-recurring gains and charges.

 

EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP financial measures and should not be considered as a substitute for net income (loss), operating income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) or as an alternative to net cash provided by operating activities as a measure of CRI’s profitability or liquidity. CRI’s management believes EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are useful financial metrics because they allow external users of CRI’s financial statements, such as industry analysts, investors, lenders and rating agencies, to more effectively evaluate CRI’s operating performance, compare the results of its operations from period to period and against CRI’s peers and because it highlights trends in CRI’s business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on GAAP measures. CRI also presents EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA because it believes EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are important supplemental measures of its performance that are frequently used by others in evaluating companies in its industry. Because EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA exclude some, but not all, items that affect net income (loss) and may vary among companies, the EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA CRI presents may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.
